covers.quote: Use the ellipsis:
if you omit words in quoted text
to mark an unfinished phrase, clause or sentence.
If a paragraph or more is omitted from a block quotation, you can place the ellipsis on a line of its own.

examples.note: Quoted text with omitted words.

parts.quote: The report is well written, but it needs a thorough review … There is an obvious need for more work.

examples.note: Unfinished quoted wording.

parts.quote: Whitlam’s speech on the steps of Parliament House (‘Well may we say …’) is still widely quoted.

examples.note: The ellipsis stands on its own line for an omitted paragraph or more.

parts.quote: The review clarified that the Army might have to fight on home ground.
During exercises, ADF personnel were tasked with tracking down enemy troops from the mythical nation of Musoria.

rules.quote: Show missing words or ideas with ellipses
rules.violation_condition: An omission within quoted text, or an unfinished phrase, clause or sentence, is not marked with an ellipsis.
when: Applies when words are omitted within quoted text.
Applies when marking an unfinished phrase, clause or sentence.
If a paragraph or more is omitted from a block quotation, the ellipsis may appear on a line of its own.
rules.why: G-2 keeps the two uses as conditions of one omission-marker rule; G-3 treats standalone placement as a permission.

examples.note: The annotation follows the quote in square brackets.

parts.quote: The minister wrote, ‘The policy settings were … comprehensive’ [ellipsis in original].

rules.quote: If there is an ellipsis in the original text you’re quoting, add the phrase ‘ellipsis in original’ in square brackets after the quote.
rules.violation_condition: A quotation containing an ellipsis from the original source lacks the annotation [ellipsis in original] after the quote, or presents that annotation without square brackets.
when: The ellipsis is present in the original source, rather than introduced to mark an omission by the person quoting it.
Determining whether the ellipsis is original requires access to the source.
rules.why: One required annotation produces one finding; its wording, brackets and position belong to that check.

rules.quote: Use the same font as the surrounding text.
rules.violation_condition: The [ellipsis in original] annotation uses a different font from the surrounding text.
when: Applies to the bracketed annotation identifying an ellipsis in the original source.
Checking requires font information, not just plain text.
rules.why: The font requirement is independent of whether the annotation is present and correctly worded.

when: A question mark or exclamation mark may follow an ellipsis if necessary.

rules.quote: Use a single space before and after each ellipsis.
rules.specification: Following the Correct example, exempt a terminal ellipsis immediately before a closing quotation mark from the following-space requirement. Also exempt line boundaries around a permitted standalone ellipsis. The explicit question-mark and exclamation-mark exception requires no intervening space.
rules.violation_condition: An ellipsis lacks the required single-space separation from surrounding text, has multiple separating spaces, or is separated by a space from a following final question mark or exclamation mark.
when: Normally require one space before and after the ellipsis.
Do not insert a space between the ellipsis and a following final question mark or exclamation mark.
A terminal ellipsis may directly precede a closing quotation mark, as shown in the Correct example.
An ellipsis representing an omitted paragraph or more may stand alone on a line.
rules.why: G-4 selects the precise body instruction; G-2 keeps spacing exceptions in the same rule, with example-derived boundary handling made explicit.

examples.note: The question mark follows the ellipsis.

rules.quote: Include the final punctuation mark after the ellipsis.
rules.violation_condition: A quotation ending with an ellipsis lacks its required final question mark or exclamation mark after the ellipsis, including when that mark has instead been placed before it.
when: The quote ends in a question mark or exclamation mark and has a terminal ellipsis.
rules.why: E-2 identifies an instruction after example labels; retaining final punctuation is a different check from spacing it.

rules.specification: The page gives no count, density or other threshold for excessive use. A reviewer must resolve what ‘sparingly’ means in context; no numerical threshold has been invented.
rules.violation_condition: A text contains excessive or repeatedly distracting use of ellipses.
rules.why: This concerns an observable property of the text, not a writer’s workflow; its undefined threshold must remain visible rather than be invented.

rules.quote: Don’t change the original intent of quoted material
rules.violation_condition: Omissions from quoted material remove important details or misrepresent the original source’s intent.
when: Applies to omissions from quoted material represented by ellipses.
Assessment requires comparison with the original source, including important context.
rules.why: G-4 consolidates repeated instructions; G-2 treats omission of important details as a case of the same quotation-fidelity check.
